## MEGAHIT

### Introduction

MEGAHIT is an assembler for short reads, such as Illumina reads. It turns reads into contigs, longer stretches of DNA. MEGAHIT is fast, which makes it a common choice to assemble large and complex metagenomes [@li2015].

For more information, please visit [the GitHub page](https://github.com/voutcn/megahit).

For a tutorial that uses MEGAHIT, see [Assembling a metagenome](https://ndombrowski.github.io/Assembly_tutorial/).

### Installation

Installed on Crunchomics: Yes, MEGAHIT v1.2.9 is installed and available without activating a conda environment. You can check the version with:

```{bash}
megahit --version
```

```
MEGAHIT v1.2.9
```

If you want to install it yourself, the command below installs the version verified on Crunchomics. Before running it, check the tool's [GitHub](https://github.com/voutcn/megahit) for a newer version and swap the version number if one is available.

```{bash}
mamba create -n megahit_1.2.9
mamba install -n megahit_1.2.9 -c bioconda megahit=1.2.9
mamba activate megahit_1.2.9
```

### Usage

Required inputs:

-   Paired-end reads: two fastq files per sample, R1 and R2 (forward and reverse reads). The files can be compressed (`.fastq.gz`)

Generated output, in the output folder that you give with `-o`:

-   `final.contigs.fa`: the assembled contigs
-   `log`: the log of the run. Read it if a run fails
-   `done`: an empty file that MEGAHIT writes as the very last step of a run. If it is there, the run finished

```{bash}
megahit -1 data/s1_R1.fastq.gz -2 data/s1_R2.fastq.gz -t 8 -o results/assembly/s1
```

Basic options, for a full list run `megahit --help`:

-   `-1` and `-2`: the R1 and R2 files of one sample
-   `-t`: the number of threads (CPUs) to use. Match it to `--cpus-per-task` in your SLURM job script
-   `-o`: the output folder. MEGAHIT makes this folder itself, and stops with an error if it already exists. So don't make it beforehand with `mkdir`, only the folder above it (here `results/assembly`)

### Running MEGAHIT on many samples

To run MEGAHIT on many samples in a SLURM job array, and to skip the samples that already finished when you submit the job again, use the `done` file as the check. [When a tool makes its own final file](https://scienceparkstudygroup.github.io/ibed-bioinformatics-page/source/core_tools/bash-skip-finished-samples.html#when-a-tool-makes-its-own-final-file) on the page "Skip finished samples safely" shows how, and what to do with the output folder of a crashed run.

### Restarting a crashed run

If a run crashed, for example because the job ran out of time, MEGAHIT can pick it up where it stopped with the option `--continue`. Then you don't need to delete the output folder of the crashed run first. The log shows the finished steps as `passing check point`:

```{bash}
megahit -1 data/s2_R1.fastq.gz -2 data/s2_R2.fastq.gz -t 8 -o results/assembly/s2 --continue
```

What I found when I tested `--continue` on a small sample:

-   The resumed run gave the same number and total length of contigs as a run without a crash
-   MEGAHIT prints "Ignore all options except for -o/--out-dir", so it uses the settings of the first run. You can't change, for example, the number of threads on a rerun
-   On a run that already finished, `--continue` stopped with an error, because MEGAHIT deletes its temporary files at the end of a run. The finished results were not damaged, but the task failed
-   On a new sample, MEGAHIT prints "Cannot find .../options.json, switching to normal mode" and does a normal first run with the settings you give it. So in a job script, you can use `--continue` for every sample, after the skip check on `done`

*Last tested: 2026-11-10 (MEGAHIT v1.2.9 on Crunchomics).*

For what to check before you rely on the resume option of any tool, see [Tools that can resume a crashed run](https://scienceparkstudygroup.github.io/ibed-bioinformatics-page/source/core_tools/bash-skip-finished-samples.html#tools-that-can-resume-a-crashed-run).
